It enters the live Engine's POST /recommendations through the session `engine` fixture, and enters similarity-cache.db through a read-only `sqlite3.connect(f\"file:{path}?mode=ro\", uri=True)`. As a control, the cached rows are fewer than 48 before the request. The test asserts that limit=48 returns 48 rows, distinct by (video_uuid, instance_domain) and by video_id::instance_domain, and that the seed's rows in similarity_sources and similarity_items are equal before and after. `test_home_and_search_are_unchanged_by_an_upnext_fallback_and_nprobe_is_restored` runs `q=music&limit=20` search, then a linux up-next request, then the same search again, and asserts the two searches return equal ordered keys with 20 rows. It asserts that home POST /recommendations {} returns BATCH_SIZE rows with seed.mode == \"home\". It also asserts that at least one `[similar-server] ann_fallback` log message exists and that every one reports restored_nprobe == str(DEFAULT_NPROBE); the log is read from engine.db_path as in phase 1. The rewritten test_similar exclude test, the seeded test_dislike_profile pair and the four pinned rewrites (test_blocks, test_dislikes, test_frontend_blocks, test_frontend_videos, using conftest's `upnext_pool`/`pin_upnext`) land here and must pass. Each live-Engine file runs in its own validate_tests.py invocation because of the 60 requests / 60 s rate limit.</checkpoint>\n<name>Up-next pool with floored ANN fallback</name>\n<intent>`get_upnext_candidates` in data/similarity_candidates.py replaces `get_similar_candidates` in the up-next handler. When the cache is short, it fills the pool past one batch with `search_similar_above` in data/ann.py, which floors the hits and restores nprobe under index_lock. The similarity cache is never written, and home and search on the shared index keep the startup nprobe.</intent>\n<clause_1>An up-next request for a seed whose cached entry holds fewer than 48 rows returns 48 unique rows, and the seed's similarity-cache.db entry is unchanged by the request.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>After an up-next fallback, search and home return what they returned before, and every fallback search reports the shared index's nprobe restored to DEFAULT_NPROBE.</clause_2>\n<files>engine/server/data/ann.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/server.py (EDITED), engine/server/data/similarity_candidates.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py (EDITED), tests/active/conftest.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_upnext_diversity.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_similar.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_dislike_profile.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_blocks.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_dislikes.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_frontend_blocks.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_frontend_videos.py (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n<phase n=\"3\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>In test_upnext_diversity.py, `test_ten_refreshes_of_one_seed_draw_different_pages_above_the_tail_floor` enters the live Engine's POST /recommendations?id=\u2026&amp;host=\u2026&amp;limit=8&amp;debug=1 for the linux seed, through the session `engine` fixture, with body {}. It makes 10 unseeded requests and asserts each returns 8 rows, the mean pairwise Jaccard of the key sets is below 0.5, and every row's debug similarity_score is \u2265 SIMILAR_VIDEO_TAIL_MIN_SCORE \u2212 1e-6. As a control, the same path with &amp;seed=11 sent twice must return equal ordered key lists. The full suite, including the pinned rewrites from phase 2, must stay green now that the draws are random.</checkpoint>\n<name>Weighted draw from the top-M window</name>\n<intent>`_handle_seed_with_embedding` in handlers/similar.py serves an up-next page as a score-weighted Efraimidis\u2013Spirakis sample of `limit` rows from the top SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR\u00d7limit rows of the pool. The sample is random per request by default and reproducible when a `seed` query parameter is given.</intent>\n<clause_1>Ten unseeded requests for one seed return pages with mean pairwise Jaccard below 0.5, every row at or above the tail floor.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>Two requests carrying the same `seed` return the same ordered page.</clause_2>\n<files>engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_upnext_diversity.py (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n<phase n=\"4\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>In test_upnext_diversity.py, `test_upnext_with_and_without_likes_both_diversify_and_liked_rows_stay_above_the_floor` enters the live Engine's POST /videos/similar?\u2026&amp;limit=8&amp;debug=1 (a separate rate bucket) for the linux seed. It sends 10 requests with body {\"likes\": five \"music\" search rows as {uuid, host}} and 10 with {}. It asserts that each set has mean Jaccard below 0.5 and that every row drawn with likes has similarity_score \u2265 0.25. It also asserts that at least one `upnext_pool` log message after these requests has likes_rerank=yes; the log is read from engine.db_path. `test_home_and_search_are_unchanged_\u2026` gains a second assertion: at least one `upnext_pool` message has steps other than `none`, and every such message has restored_nprobe == str(DEFAULT_NPROBE).</checkpoint>\n<name>Likes-weighted draw and upnext_pool line</name>\n<intent>rerank_related_videos stamps each candidate's final score under `personalized_score`. When likes are present, up-next uses that stamp as the draw weight and the page order. Every up-next request writes one `[similar-server][id] upnext_pool` line reporting the pool, the fallback steps, the restored nprobe, the sampling mode, the window, whether likes reranked it, and the rows returned.</intent>\n<clause_1>Up-next draws made with likes and draws made without likes each diversify across refreshes; rows drawn with likes stay at or above the tail floor, and the log reports likes_rerank=yes.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>Every upnext_pool line that records fallback steps reports restored_nprobe equal to DEFAULT_NPROBE.</clause_2>\n<files>engine/server/api/recommendations/related_personalization.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_upnext_diversity.py (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n</phases>\n\n<needs_coordination>\nnone\n</needs_coordination>\n\n<rationale>\nThe phases follow the plan's own seams: config (R1), the pool and its fallback (R2/R3), the draw (R4), then likes and the log line (R5/R6). Each phase ends with the full suite green and is verified against the live Engine through the session `engine` fixture (conftest.py:106), which also provides the Engine log at `engine.db_path`. That log is the only place the startup line, the restored nprobe and likes_rerank can be observed without an in-process test the draft did not ask for.\n\nThe split between phases 2 and 3 is deliberate. Phase 2 swaps in `get_upnext_candidates` but keeps today's deterministic `rows[:limit]` and today's rerank of the page, so the fill, cache-immutability and nprobe-isolation claims are verified before any randomness exists.\n\nThe rewrites of the existing tests (test_similar exclude, seeded test_dislike_profile, and the four pinned gateway tests with the conftest helpers) land in phase 2, not phase 3. Two reasons: the deeper pool can already break the page-depth assumptions in those tests, and pinning (the window no larger than limit is served whole) and the `seed` parameter (ignored until phase 3) hold in both regimes. So the suite never goes red between phases.\n\nPhase 3 introduces the window and the Efraimidis\u2013Spirakis draw and moves the existing rerank onto the window. Phase 4 adds the additive `personalized_score` stamp as the draw weight and the single upnext_pool line.\n\nOne named departure from draft \u00a77d test 5, which the operator approved: in phase 2 the restored nprobe is read from ann.py's `ann_fallback` line, because the upnext_pool line does not exist until phase 4. Phase 4 then asserts it on upnext_pool exactly as the draft specifies.\n\nNo prose phase: every text change in this build (the OVERVIEW, README and ADR-level docs, issues and plans) is documentation, updated at Step 9. The {principles}, {shape_ladder-ladder} and {tdd_seams} placeholders reached this step unfilled, as the ladder did in the drafting step. The seams above are therefore taken from the existing harness precedents (spec_from_file_location config reads in test_similar, live Engine requests and the log file from the `engine` fixture, read-only sqlite for the cache).\n</rationale>",
    "author:tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py": "<items>\n<item id=\"C2b\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>An earlier round of this remediation added two assertions that carry \"carries ONE ... line\"; this turn changes no bytes. (1) tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:172, `assert len(messages) == len(_messages(engine.db_path, NPROBE_PREFIX))`, requires the session log to have exactly as many upnext_config lines as `[similar-server] ann_nprobe_configured=` lines. set_nprobe logs that line once for each start that loads the index, so the count means \"one per start\" even when the fixture retries into the same log. This rules out a line logged twice per start (2N against N) and a line logged on every request (the count grows past N). (2) :181, `assert [_tokens(message) for message in variant_messages] == [sorted(VARIANT_LOG_TOKENS.items())]`, runs one fresh Engine start with the constants overridden and requires a list with exactly one element. A second copy of the line makes it a two-element list, and the assertion fails. :179 arms it by requiring exactly one `ann_nprobe_configured=25` line in that log. The claim auditor's re-audit marks C2b CARRIED at :172 and :181.</what>\n</item>\n</items>\n\n<findings_addressed>\nShape CRITICAL 1 (hardcoded-spec-mirror at :152/:155/:157): kept, because the operator decided to keep them. The auditor passed this to the dispatcher because C1 is a must_prove claim about the default values themselves. Neither of the rule's alternatives can carry it: how the constants are used only arrives in Phases 2-4, and a shared source file would check that the file loads, not the values. I asked in this session with AskUser, offering \"Keep the literal pins\", \"Narrow C1 to use only\" and \"Stop\". The operator's answer was \"keep\". The comment at line 34 records that decision. How the constants are used is still tested at :163 (TARGET_MIN_POOL follows BATCH_SIZE at 64) and :181 (the startup line follows the module at overridden values).\nShape RECOMMENDATION 1 (substring count on server_config.py source at :160): not taken. The recommendation does not block. The count only exists to guard the text rewrite at :161. If the file is reformatted, it fails loudly at a supporting assertion; it never passes silently.\n</findings_addressed>\n\n<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:152 \u2014 the eight SIMILAR_VIDEO_* constants other than TARGET_MIN_POOL are read from server_config.py, loaded from its file. Each must equal {name: (type, value)}: SEARCH_LIMIT int 5000, TOP_K int 300, NPROBE int 32, MAX_NPROBE int 128, MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT int 20000, MIN_SCORE float 0.35, TAIL_MIN_SCORE float 0.25, SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR int 4. The operator chose to keep these literal pins (\"keep\").</assertion>\n<expected>Each name maps to (its type, its default). Today's run fails here with every name reading (NoneType, None).</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>If a constant is missing or misnamed it reads (NoneType, None). If it is left at a sibling value (NPROBE = DEFAULT_NPROBE) it reads (int, 24). If it has the wrong type (SEARCH_LIMIT = 5000.0) it reads (float, 5000.0). Each of these fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:153 and :155 \u2014 module.BATCH_SIZE == 48, and SIMILAR_VIDEO_TARGET_MIN_POOL is (int, 48)</assertion>\n<expected>BATCH_SIZE is 48 (already true today); TARGET_MIN_POOL is (int, 48)</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>If TARGET_MIN_POOL is missing, set to another pool size (TOP_K 300), or a float 48.0, it reads (NoneType, None), (int, 300) or (float, 48.0), and the assertion fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:163 \u2014 server_config.py is loaded again with the home profile's `\"batch_size\": 48,` rewritten to 64, and its SIMILAR_VIDEO_TARGET_MIN_POOL must be 64. It is guarded by :160 (the literal occurs twice) and :162 (the variant's BATCH_SIZE == 64).</assertion>\n<expected>64</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A hard-coded `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TARGET_MIN_POOL = 48`, or one taken from guest_home's batch_size, still reads 48 in the variant, and the assertion fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:157 \u2014 RELATED_VIDEOS_PERSONALIZATION's (alpha, beta) == (0.7, 0.3)</assertion>\n<expected>(0.7, 0.3)</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>If the current alpha 0.2 / beta 0.8 is left in place, or the two weights are swapped, it reads (0.2, 0.8) or (0.3, 0.7), and the assertion fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:170 \u2014 the session Engine's log (engine.db_path) has at least one JSON `message` starting `[similar-server] upnext_config`. The test polls for it for 5 s.</assertion>\n<expected>A non-empty list</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>If the constants are defined but never logged at startup, or are logged under another prefix, the list is [] and the assertion fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:172 \u2014 the session log has as many upnext_config messages as `[similar-server] ann_nprobe_configured=` messages. This carries \"ONE ... line\" per start.</assertion>\n<expected>Equal counts: 1 and 1 when the Engine started on the first try; n and n if the fixture retried.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>If the line is logged twice per start, or on every request that reaches the server, there are more upnext lines than nprobe lines, and the assertion fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:174 \u2014 for every upnext_config message in the session log, the sorted NAME=value pairs equal exactly the nine default tokens</assertion>\n<expected>[('SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_NPROBE','128'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT','20000'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_MIN_SCORE','0.35'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_NPROBE','32'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR','4'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_SEARCH_LIMIT','5000'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_TAIL_MIN_SCORE','0.25'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_TARGET_MIN_POOL','48'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_TOP_K','300')]</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>Any of these gives a different pair list and fails: a line with only eight names, lower-case names, a duplicated name, a value formatted differently (5000.0), or the ANN's nprobe 24 where 32 belongs.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:181 \u2014 an Engine started with the nine SIMILAR_VIDEO_* constants overridden on its server_config module logs exactly one upnext_config line, and its sorted tokens equal the override values. This is armed by :179 (the variant's nprobe line reads `ann_nprobe_configured=25`) and by `_start_variant`'s check that the lifecycle start line was reached.</assertion>\n<expected>[[('SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_NPROBE','129'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT','20001'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_MIN_SCORE','0.36'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_NPROBE','33'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR','5'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_SEARCH_LIMIT','5001'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_TAIL_MIN_SCORE','0.26'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_TARGET_MIN_POOL','49'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_TOP_K','301')]]</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>If server.py logs a hard-coded string of the defaults instead of reading server_config, this assertion sees the default tokens and fails. If the line is logged twice per start, the list has two elements and fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n</rows>\n\n<answers>\n1. Absence only: no. Nothing asserts that something is absent. The count at :172 comes after :170, which needs at least one line. The variant check at :181 is armed by :179 and by `_start_variant`'s check that the lifecycle start line was reached.\n2. Echoed literal: no. No assertion compares a value with itself, and none recomputes production's transformation. The expected log tokens are literal strings, not str() of a module value. Deleting the SIMILAR_VIDEO_* assignments in server_config.py turns :152 red. Deleting the startup upnext_config logging in server.py turns :170 and :181 red. Hard-coding that line's values turns :181 red. The literal pins at :152/:155/:157 are the shape finding, and the operator's answer on them was \"keep\".\n3. One value: no. The log is read at the defaults and at nine values that differ from them (:174 and :181). TARGET_MIN_POOL is read at batch sizes 48 and 64 (:155 and :163).\n4. The double: no. Nothing stands in for a project module. The variant runs the real server.py and the real server_config.py from its file, with attributes overridden on that module.\n5. It collects: yes. This turn changed no bytes; I re-read the file and :172 and :181 are where the item says they are. The last ValidateTests run collected the test and failed inside it.\n6. Observed, not predicted: yes. This turn adds no expectation. The premises behind the existing expectations were observed in earlier probe runs. The contents of the upnext_config line itself cannot be observed until the phase writes it.\n7. Still red for its own reason: yes. The file is unchanged since the last ValidateTests run, which failed at :152, the first C1 assertion, with the SIMILAR_VIDEO_* constants reading (NoneType, None) because Phase 1 has not been built. Three probe files still need deleting, and I have no delete tool: tests/tmp/probe_09_variant_start.py, tests/tmp/probe_09_variant.py, tests/tmp/probe_09_engine_log.py.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "self_check:tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py": "<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py:74 \u2014 the eight SIMILAR_VIDEO_* constants other than TARGET_MIN_POOL, read from server_config.py loaded from its file, equal {name: (type, value)} for SEARCH_LIMIT int 5000, TOP_K int 300, NPROBE int 32, MAX_NPROBE int 128, MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT int 20000, MIN_SCORE float 0.35, TAIL_MIN_SCORE float 0.25, SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR int 4</assertion>\n<expected>Each name maps to (its type, its default) exactly as listed. The parser was observed on a sample message in probe_09_variant.py.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A line that logs only eight names (e.g. drops TARGET_MIN_POOL), uses lower-case names like the other startup lines (`top_k=300`), logs one name twice, or logs a different value (the ANN's configured nprobe 24 instead of 32) gives a different sorted pair list and fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n</rows>\n\n<answers>\n1. Whole claim. Before the rewrite: no, in part. Every name, type and value in C1 was pinned. But \"TARGET_MIN_POOL equal to BATCH_SIZE\" was only checked at 48, and C2's \"nine tokens\" went through a dict that would have collapsed a duplicated name. After the rewrite, C1 is carried by :74, :75, :77, :79 and :85 (the variant load with batch_size 64). C2 is carried by :92 (the line exists) and :96 (exactly nine pairs, sorted, so a duplicate shows). C2 says \"one line\". The test asserts at least one, and that every copy carries the defaults. It does not assert exactly one, because the `engine` fixture retries failed starts into the same log (conftest.py:118), so an aborted attempt can add a second line. The docstring now matches what is asserted.\n2. Absence only. No. Nothing asserts that something is absent. Of the variant-load controls, :82 was observed passing in the probe and the variant's BATCH_SIZE came out 64 there. :92 is itself the positive check for :96's loop, which cannot pass with no messages.\n3. Echoed literal. Yes before the rewrite. The expected log tokens were `str(getattr(module, name))`, which is the same str() conversion production would apply to the same module values. They are now literal strings (EXPECTED_LOG_TOKENS). Production lines whose deletion turns each assertion red: the SIMILAR_VIDEO_* assignments in server_config.py turn :74 red, the alpha/beta values in RELATED_VIDEOS_PERSONALIZATION turn :79 red, TARGET_MIN_POOL's `= BATCH_SIZE` turns :77/:85 red, and the startup `logging.info(\"[similar-server] upnext_config ...\")` in server.py turns :92 red.\n4. One value. Yes before the rewrite. TARGET_MIN_POOL was compared against BATCH_SIZE, a sibling from the same module, at the single value 48, so a hard-coded 48 passed. The rewrite loads server_config.py a second time with the home profile's `\"batch_size\": 48,` changed to 64 and asserts TARGET_MIN_POOL == 64 (:85). The other constants are fixed defaults with no input to vary.\n5. The double. No. Nothing is replaced with a stand-in. The real server_config.py is executed from its file, and the real Engine subprocess is started by the session `engine` fixture.\n6. It collects. Yes. The given `--collect-only` output reads \"no tests\" in the summary, but tests/last_test_output.txt from that run says `1 test collected`, which is the one test written. After the rewrite the checkpoint run shows `collected 1 item`. `ROOT` and `engine` import from tests/active/conftest.py. `engine.db_path` is a Path to the log (probe: `db_path /tmp/.../engine0/engine.log <class 'pathlib.PosixPath'>`).\n7. Observed, not predicted. Yes, now. probe_09_engine_log.py showed the log format: JSON lines with a `message` field of the form `[similar-server] name=value ...`, e.g. `\"message\":\"[similar-server] ann_nprobe_configured=24 index_type=IndexIDMap2 ivf_type=IndexIVF\"`, and no upnext_config line yet. probe_09_variant.py showed the variant's premises: `count 2`, `base 48 variant 64 guest_home 48 home 64`, and the token parser producing `[('SIMILAR_VIDEO_MIN_SCORE', '0.35'), ('SIMILAR_VIDEO_TOP_K', '300')]`. That probe first failed on a wrong premise: I had assumed the second literal was in an `upnext` profile (`KeyError: 'batch_size'`). Reading server_config.py:162 showed it is `guest_home`, and the test comment was corrected. The exact contents of the upnext_config line cannot be observed until the phase logs it; the expected pairs come from the clause's defaults. The two probe files could not be deleted because I have no delete tool; tests/tmp/probe_09_variant.py and tests/tmp/probe_09_engine_log.py should be removed.\n8. Red, not green. Yes, it fails. ValidateTests reported `tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1.py  1 failed`, `[exit status 1]`.\n9. Red for the right reason. Yes.     "step_7_implement:2": "<changes>\n### `engine/server/data/ann.py`\n- Moved the nprobe code here from `server.py` and split it into four functions. `_extract_ivf` returns the object from `faiss.extract_index_ivf`, or None. `get_nprobe` reads nprobe from that object. `apply_nprobe` is the setter that writes without logging, keeping the old `hasattr` branches. `set_nprobe` is the startup wrapper, and its `ann_nprobe_configured=... index_type=... ivf_type=...` log line is byte-identical to before. The reader, the setter and the restore all use the same IVF object.\n- Added `search_similar_above(server, seed, nprobe, search_limit, min_score)` right after `compute_similar_items`. It holds one `server.index_lock` for the whole search: it reads the current nprobe, sets the requested one, searches, and restores the old value in a `finally`. It then reads nprobe back from the index. After that it drops ids \u2264 0, the seed's rowid and any hit below `min_score`. It logs `[similar-server] ann_fallback nprobe= search_limit= floor= hits= restored_nprobe=` and fetches metadata only for the hits that are left. It returns `{video_id, instance_domain, score}` entries in score order, with no author cap, plus the restored nprobe. The IDs are still rowids, so plan 17 has one more function to migrate.\n- `compute_similar_items` and `search_index` are unchanged.\n\n### `engine/server/api/server.py`\n- Deleted the local `set_nprobe` and imported it with `from data.ann import set_nprobe`. The startup call is unchanged. `import faiss` stays, because `faiss.read_index` and the `faiss.Index` annotation still use it.\n\n### `engine/server/data/similarity_candidates.py`\n- The module comment now describes the two entry points: `get_similar_candidates` for home, which can compute and write the cache, and `get_upnext_candidates` for up-next, which only reads the cache and never writes it.\n- New `UpnextPoolPolicy` dataclass holding the pool size, the floors and the fallback caps.\n- New `get_upnext_candidates(server, seed, policy, excluded, request_id)`, which returns `(rows, stats)`. Step by step:\n  - It reads the cache with `require_full=False, allow_write=False`, using read limit `max(cache_limit, top_k)`.\n  - It drops cached entries below the tail floor and sorts the rest by score.\n  - `_upnext_rows` builds the pool: floor, then `_build_rows` capped at `top_k`, then the request's exclude keys, then `apply_serving_moderation_filters`.\n  - If the pool is below target, or the cache had no entry, it steps nprobe and search_limit by doubling up to the caps. It stops at the target, when both caps are reached, or when a step adds nothing.\n  - Hits at 0.35 or above are merged with the cached entries; on a `like_key` clash the cached copy wins. The tail (0.25 and up, from the last search) is added only if the pool is still short.\n  - A final pass dedupes by `(video_uuid, instance_domain)` and `like_key`, then cuts to `top_k`.\n  - `_write_cache` and `_compute_candidates` cannot be reached from this function.\n- New private helpers: `_upnext_rows`, `_merge_entries`, `_sorted_by_score`, `_dedup_rows`. `get_similar_candidates` and the helpers it already had are unchanged.\n\n### `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py`\n- `_handle_seed_with_embedding` builds an `UpnextPoolPolicy` from the `SIMILAR_VIDEO_*` constants, which are now imported, plus `similar_per_like` as the cache read limit and `refresh_cache`. It calls `get_upnext_candidates` with `fetch_request_excluded_keys()` and the request id, in place of `get_similar_candidates`.\n- The exclude filter that ran after scoring is gone, because the pool build now applies it. Scoring, the dislike penalty, `rows[:limit]` and the personalization rerank are otherwise unchanged; the draw is phase 3.\n- Removed the imports this left unused: `SimilarityCandidatesPolicy`, `get_similar_candidates` and `like_key`.\n\n### Test files listed for this phase but not edited\n- I did not touch `tests/active/conftest.py`, `test_upnext_diversity.py`, `test_similar.py`, `test_dislike_profile.py`, `test_blocks.py`, `test_dislikes.py`, `test_frontend_blocks.py` or `test_frontend_videos.py`. This step is production code only, as in phase 1, and these are durable tests that have already gated. They need their own step.\n- One of them breaks as of this phase: `test_frontend_videos.py` expects an empty batch within 6 batches of 8, and the linux pool now holds at least 48 rows. The others are still deterministic until the phase 3 draw lands, so I expect them to hold for now.\n\n### Observed with a probe (`tests/tmp/probe_09_phase2_pool.py`, live Engine)\n- For both seeds, linux and cooking, each request returned 200 at limit 48, 30 and 8, with every row distinct on both keys. The lowest `similarity_score` on any page was 0.73 for linux and 0.51 for cooking. Each request took about 0.2 s.\n- Each fallback logged `nprobe=32 search_limit=5000 floor=0.25 hits=4999 restored_nprobe=24`, and the startup line reads `ann_nprobe_configured=24 index_type=IndexIDMap2 ivf_type=IndexIVF`.\n- I have no tool that deletes files, so the probe file is still on disk and needs removing.\n- I did not run the checkpoint itself.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\ntests/tmp/probe_09_phase2_pool.py - a throwaway probe of the live up-next pool and fallback log. It is still on disk because I have no tool that deletes files, and it needs removing.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

    "self_check:tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase3.py": "<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase3.py:65 \u2014 the mean pairwise Jaccard of the key sets of ten unseeded pages for the linux seed is below 0.5 (MAX_MEAN_JACCARD). Lines 69 and 73 stop an empty or short page from passing either comparison without measuring anything.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n</rows>\n\n<answers>\n1. Whole claim \u2014 no. The docstring's C1 bullet is carried by lines 60, 61, 62 and 65. Its C2 bullet (same page for &seed=11 sent twice, a different page for &seed=12) is carried by lines 69, 70, 73 and 74. Both must_prove clauses are asserted.\n2. Absence only \u2014 yes, found and rewritten. Line 72 used to be a bare `!=` between the seed=12 page and the seed=11 page, so an empty or short seed=12 page would have passed it without measuring anything. I bound that page to `other` and added `assert len(other) == PAGE_LIMIT` on line 73 as the control, with the `!=` now on line 74. Line 70's equality is armed by line 69. Line 62's `all(...)` is armed by line 60, which requires 8 rows.\n3. Echoed literal \u2014 no. The test computes Jaccard over what the server returns, which is its own measure and not production's transformation. Each assertion has a production line that turns it red: the rows[:limit] slice at similar.py:824 turns line 65 red today, and an implementation that ignores the seed turns line 70 red.\n4. The test runs against the real session Engine subprocess from tests/active/conftest.py, with nothing faked.\n6. It collects \u2014 yes. The first collect-only run printed \"no tests\" with exit 0. That line is how the runner summarises a collect-only run, and exit 5 also folds to green, so it was not proof. The real run printed \"collected 1 item\". The conftest import resolves, `engine` binds as the session fixture, and ClientBackend.request accepts (method, path, headers, body) as called.\n7. Observed, not predicted \u2014 yes, with one prediction called out. Observed in the run: a numeric debug similarity_score on each row that meets the floor, 8 distinct rows, and a Jaccard of 1.0 for the fixed page. The floor value is read from server_config.py at run time rather than hard-coded. The comment's ~0.14 comes from an offline simulation and is labelled as such; no assertion depends on it.\n8. It fails at \"tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase3.py:65: AssertionError\", on \"AssertionError: (1.0, [[('d63cb157-2391-4c4b-9795-ec6a0f4fbb69', 'video.linux.it'), \u2026]]) assert 1.0 < 0.5\". That is C1's own claim, reached after the controls on lines 60\u201362 passed. All ten unseeded pages are identical because the handler serves rows[:limit].\n10. Observed expected output \u2014 the C1 row matches the run, which shows 1.0 today against below 0.5 required. The run never reached the C2 lines (69\u201374) because it stopped at line 65. The C2 row says so and states only what the observed fixed top-8 implies: line 70 would hold and line 74 would be red against the current code.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:3": "<changes>\n### `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py`\n- **New `seed` query parameter.** `_handle_similar` reads it with the existing `_parse_non_negative_int` into `draw_seed`, next to the debug parse. If it is missing or not a valid integer, the draw is random, not a 400. The parse only reads the query string and touches no server attribute, so the child-process stub tests are unaffected. `draw_seed` is passed to `_handle_seed_with_embedding` as a new last parameter (`draw_seed: int | None = None`).\n- **Page is now drawn, not cut.** In `_handle_seed_with_embedding`, `rows = rows[:limit]` is replaced. After `score_and_rank_list`, the handler takes the top `min(SIMILAR_VIDEO_SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR \u00d7 limit, len(rows))` ranked rows as the window and passes it to `_draw_page`. `SIMILAR_VIDEO_SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR` is added to the `server_config` import.\n- **New `_draw_page(window, limit, draw_seed)`.** It is an Efraimidis\u2013Spirakis weighted sample without replacement:\n  - Each row with a positive `score` gets the key `log(u) / score`, and the `limit` largest keys are chosen.\n  - Rows whose score is zero or less are used only if the positive ones cannot fill the page, and then in window order.\n  - If the window holds `limit` rows or fewer, all of it is returned.\n  - The page is returned ordered by score, descending.\n  - Without a seed, `u` comes from a fresh `np.random.default_rng()` on each request, taking `1 - random()` so `log` never sees 0.\n- **New `_seeded_uniform(draw_seed, key)`.** It computes the seeded `u` from a blake2b hash of the seed and the row's `like_key`, mapped into (0, 1]. So the same seed and pool give the same page in every process, and a row keeps its draw when the rows around it change. Added imports: `hashlib`, `math` and `from recommendations.keys import like_key`.\n- **Personalization is left where it was.** `rerank_related_videos` still runs on the served page, now after the draw. The plan moves it onto the window, with the `personalized_score` stamp as the draw weight, in phase 4. Moving it without the stamp would make likes have no effect on the page at all.\n- **Deferred to phase 4:** the `upnext_pool` log line.\n\n### `tests/active/test_upnext_diversity.py`\n- Not touched. It is listed as EDITED but does not exist yet; phases 1 and 2 did not create it either. It is where the `tests/tmp` checkpoints move once they become durable tests, and this step is production code only.\n- The pinned rewrites of `test_blocks`, `test_dislikes`, `test_frontend_blocks`, `test_frontend_videos`, `test_similar` and `test_dislike_profile`, planned for phase 2, are also still unwritten. From this phase on, those tests' comparisons across unseeded up-next requests (plain pages repeating, a target reappearing on a fresh draw, plain-versus-dislike comparisons) meet random draws and are expected to fail or flake until those rewrites land.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "author:tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase4.py": "<items>\n<item id=\"D1\">\n<disposition>justified</disposition>\n<what>The prose is narrowed to what the test asserts. The module docstring's first line now reads \"Up-next draws with and without likes, and the upnext_pool log line, checked against the session Engine and one started off DEFAULT_NPROBE\". It no longer says \"likes-weighted draw\", and no other sentence claims that likes change the draw weight. The likes claims the file does make are carried: liked and plain draws each diversify (:203, :205), liked rows stay above the floor (:200), and likes_rerank reads yes or no correctly (:209, :211, :218).</what>\n</item>\n<item id=\"N3\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>The test is named `test_every_upnext_pool_line_records_the_fallback_steps_its_request_ran_and_nprobe_restored_to_default`. `_pools_with_fallbacks` pairs every upnext_pool line in the session log with the ann_fallback lines logged between that request's own `[id] start` line and its pool line. :243 asserts `_steps(line) == _searched(fallbacks)` for every line, and no longer filters out lines whose steps are `none`. The test sends its own request on each route, POST /recommendations and POST /videos/similar (:233\u2013:235), so a second request always exists even when the test runs alone. The same check runs again at :272 on the off-default Engine's two lines. The wrong implementation this excludes is any request, on either route, that ran ann_fallback searches but logged steps=none: its line gives [] against a non-empty list of searches and fails :243. The control at :239 shows both of this test's requests ran the fallback.</what>\n</item>\n</items>\n\n<findings_addressed>\nShape CRITICAL 1 (single-value-pin, :199, now :250): fixed. I added `test_on_an_engine_started_off_default_nprobe_every_upnext_pool_line_reports_the_nprobe_its_fallback_restored` (:253\u2013:274). It runs on a second real Engine, the `off_default_engine` fixture. That Engine runs the real server.py through a launcher that gives the real `set_nprobe` a startup value of OFF_DEFAULT_NPROBE = 16. Nothing else is replaced, and DEFAULT_NPROBE stays 24 in every module. :274 asserts that each upnext_pool line's restored_nprobe equals its own request's last ann_fallback read-back, and that both equal \"16\". The only way to produce that value is to relay the read-back. Two controls come first. :258 checks that the startup line reads ann_nprobe_configured=16, that 16 \u2260 DEFAULT_NPROBE, and that 16 is below R2's ladder. :265 checks that every ann_fallback read back 16. Both passed on this run. A probe had observed the same beforehand: healthy in about 1 s, and `restored_nprobe=16` on both routes. :250 stays, and still pins the session Engine's lines to DEFAULT_NPROBE as C2 words it.\nShape CRITICAL 2 (stub question, :199): fixed by the same test. Take an upnext_pool line that records the real steps but fills restored_nprobe from the DEFAULT_NPROBE constant rather than from stats[\"restored_nprobe\"]. On the off-default Engine it reads 24 against the expected 16 and fails :274. :272 also checks every line's steps against that request's own searches on this Engine.\n</findings_addressed>\n\n<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase4.py:203 and :205: the mean pairwise Jaccard of the 10 liked pages is below 0.5, and the same holds for the 10 plain pages. :198 checks that every page has 8 distinct rows.</assertion>\n<expected>Below 0.5 in both sets. A probe observed about 0.16 liked and 0.14 plain. This run passed :198\u2013:205 and then failed at :208.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>Reranking the liked window and cutting it to its top 8, or a no-likes path that serves the ranked top 8. Either repeats one page, and the Jaccard is 1.0.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase4.py:200: every row drawn with likes has a debug similarity_score of at least SIMILAR_VIDEO_TAIL_MIN_SCORE \u2212 1e-6.</assertion>\n<expected>Every score is at or above 0.25; the lowest observed was 0.7253. This run passed the line.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A likes pull that brings in rows from the liked videos' own neighbourhoods rather than from the seed's floored pool. Rows below 0.25 appear.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase4.py:208 and :209: the 10 liked requests write 10 upnext_pool lines, each with likes_rerank=yes. The control at :194 shows their likes resolved. :211 checks that the plain lines read no, and :218 that the unknown-likes line reads no; :217 is the control for :218. :212 checks that the 20 lines carry 20 distinct request ids.</assertion>\n<expected>Ten lines, each reading yes. This run fails at :208 with `assert 0 == 10`, because no upnext_pool line is written before phase 4.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>No upnext_pool line, or a missing likes_rerank token: :208/:209 fail. A hard-coded yes, or a stamp that outlives its request: :211 fails. likes_rerank keyed on the body carrying likes rather than on a rerank running: :218 fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase4.py:235, :243, :245, :248 on the session Engine. Each up-next route's request writes one upnext_pool line (:235). Every pool line in the session records exactly the (nprobe, search_limit) pairs of its own request's ann_fallback lines (:243). Each of those nprobes is on R2's ladder and above DEFAULT_NPROBE (:245). At least one line has steps other than none (:248). The control at :239 shows both requests ran the fallback.</assertion>\n<expected>One line per request, with steps such as `32/5000->N` that match the request's ann_fallback lines. This run fails at :235 with `('/recommendations', [])`, `assert 0 == 1`.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A line that prints the planned ladder or the caps, or that writes steps=none on any request that ran searches: :243 fails. Steps that log the index's current nprobe (24): :245 fails. Every line reading none: :248 fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase4.py:250 on the session Engine: every line with steps reports a restored_nprobe equal to its own request's last ann_fallback read-back, and both equal str(DEFAULT_NPROBE). The control at :227 shows the startup ann_nprobe_configured lines read DEFAULT_NPROBE.</assertion>\n<expected>\"24\" on every line with steps. The ann_fallback side was observed as restored_nprobe=24 on both routes. The pool-line side is not reached yet, because the test goes red at :235.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A line that reports the last raised nprobe (32, 64 or 128), `none`, or a missing token, or a restore that leaves the index raised: :250 fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase4.py:268, :272, :274 on an Engine started at OFF_DEFAULT_NPROBE = 16, with DEFAULT_NPROBE left at 24. Each line's restored_nprobe equals its request's last ann_fallback read-back, and both equal \"16\" (:274). The controls are :258 (ann_nprobe_configured=16, 16 \u2260 DEFAULT_NPROBE, 16 below the ladder) and :265 (every ann_fallback read back 16).</assertion>\n<expected>\"16\" on both lines. :258 and :265 passed on this run; the probe had shown `ann_fallback nprobe=32 search_limit=5000 \u2026 restored_nprobe=16` on both routes. The run fails at :268 with `('/recommendations', [])`, `assert 0 == 1`, because the line is not written yet.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A line whose restored_nprobe comes from the DEFAULT_NPROBE constant rather than from stats[\"restored_nprobe\"]: it reads \"24\" and :274 fails. A line that reports the raised step nprobe (32) or `none`: :274 fails.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n</rows>\n\n<answers>\n1. Absence only: no. The likes_rerank=no checks (:211, :218) read a positive token, and the profile controls (:195, :217) arm them. The session steps equality (:243) is armed by :239 and :248. The off-default assertions (:272, :274) are armed by :258 and :265, which passed on this run. Deleting the code under test turns :208, :235 and :268 red, which is this run.\n2. Echoed literal: no. The pool line is compared with two other sources. One is the ann_fallback line that data/ann.py:119 writes from `get_nprobe` after the restore. The other is a startup value the test chose, confirmed by the real `set_nprobe` log line. The test transforms nothing the way production does. Removing phase 4's upnext_pool logging call turns :208, :235 and :268 red. Filling restored_nprobe from DEFAULT_NPROBE instead of stats[\"restored_nprobe\"] turns :274 red.\n3. One value: that was a yes, and it is rewritten. restored_nprobe was read only at the shipped startup value, so it could only ever be DEFAULT_NPROBE. It is now read at two startup nprobes: 24 on the session Engine (:250) and 16 on the off-default Engine (:274). The two readings match only if the line relays the read-back. The likes observables are read over 10+10+1 requests; steps are read on two routes, on both Engines.\n4. The double: here is exactly what the launcher does. It swaps `data.ann.set_nprobe` for a lambda that calls the real `set_nprobe` with 16 instead of DEFAULT_NPROBE. That is the only change, and it runs once, at startup. The Engine exposes no nprobe setting, so this changes configuration; no code under test is replaced. server.py, the handler, get_upnext_candidates, search_similar_above and the log lines all run unchanged. `set_nprobe` has no other runtime caller (grep: server.py:345 only), and the real function still runs and logs ann_nprobe_configured=16.\n5. It collects: yes. \"collected 3 items\". The new imports (fcntl, os, subprocess, pytest, and BRIDGE_TOKEN, ENGINE_PY, ENGINE_SERVER, ENGINE_START_LOCK, ClientBackend and _free_port from conftest) resolved. The fixture started the Engine, and the new test reached :268.\n6. Observed, not predicted: yes for everything the test relies on now. tests/tmp/probe_09_phase4_offdefault.py showed several things. The launcher needs both engine/server and engine/server/api on sys.path; the first run, without api, failed with `No module named 'recommendations'`. The Engine was healthy in about 1 s. It logged `ann_nprobe_configured=16 index_type=IndexIDMap2 ivf_type=IndexIVF`, and `ann_fallback nprobe=32 search_limit=5000 floor=0.25 hits=4999 restored_nprobe=16` between each request's own start and done lines, on both routes. This run's :258 and :265 confirm the same inside the test. The upnext_pool line's own format still cannot be observed until phase 4 writes it; it follows the plan's _log_upnext_pool format string. I have no delete tool, so these probe files still need removing: tests/tmp/probe_09_phase4_offdefault.py, probe_09_phase4.py and probe_09_phase4_nofallback.py.\n7. Still red for its own reason: yes. There are 3 failures, each after its controls passed. :208 fails with `AssertionError: []`, `assert 0 == 10`. :235 fails with `('/recommendations', [])`, `assert 0 == 1`. :268 fails with `('/recommendations', [])`, `assert 0 == 1`, after :258 and :265 passed on the 16-nprobe Engine.     "step_7_implement:4": "<changes>\n### `engine/server/api/recommendations/related_personalization.py`\n- New module constant `PERSONALIZED_SCORE_KEY = \"personalized_score\"`.\n- `rerank_related_videos` now writes each candidate's `final_score` under that key, in the scoring loop. It still returns the same candidates in the same order. The early returns (no user, no likes, no embeddings) leave no stamp.\n- Updated the module comment: the function now also stamps the score, up-next runs it on the top-M window before the draw, and the stamp is the draw weight and the page order.\n\n### `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py`\n- `rerank_related_videos` now runs on the top-M window before `_draw_page`. It used to run on the page after the draw. `likes_reranked` is true only when a row in the window has the stamp. Likes that resolve to no videos therefore log `no`, even when the request body carried likes. The `timing personalize` line is unchanged.\n- New `_draw_weight(row)` returns `personalized_score` if the row has one, else `score`. `_draw_page` uses it for both the Efraimidis\u2013Spirakis key and the final page order. Before, both used `score` directly. A window of `limit` rows or fewer still comes back whole and in window order; the rerank has already sorted it by the stamp.\n- `get_upnext_candidates`' stats are now kept (`pool_stats`); they used to be discarded.\n- New `_log_upnext_pool(request_id, stats, draw_seed, window_size, likes_reranked, page)` writes one line per up-next request: `[similar-server][<id>] upnext_pool initial= steps= restored_nprobe= final= tail= sampling=random|seeded window= likes_rerank=yes|no returned=`.\n  - `steps` lists each search that ran as `nprobe/search_limit->pool`, comma-joined, or `none` if no search ran.\n  - `restored_nprobe` is `stats[\"restored_nprobe\"]`, the value the last `search_similar_above` call read back from the index. It is `none` when no search ran. It is never filled from `DEFAULT_NPROBE`.\n  - The line is written after the draw and before the response. The empty-pool branch writes it too, with window 0 and returned 0.\n- Imports `PERSONALIZED_SCORE_KEY` next to `rerank_related_videos`.\n\n### Probe of the implemented phase (`tests/tmp/probe_09_phase4_impl.py`)\nOne linux request to POST /videos/similar with five \"music\" likes, one with no likes, one whose likes name no known video, then one POST /recommendations. All four returned 200 with 8 rows, and every row's debug similarity_score was 0.725 or higher. Each request logged exactly one line, for example `[similar-server][37d4d1] upnext_pool initial=18 steps=32/5000->300 restored_nprobe=24 final=300 tail=0 sampling=random window=32 likes_rerank=yes returned=8`. `likes_rerank` read `yes` on the liked request and `no` on the other three, and each line came after its request's own `ann_fallback` line. I did not run the checkpoint itself.\n\n### `tests/active/test_upnext_diversity.py`\n- Not touched. It is listed as EDITED but still does not exist; phases 1\u20133 did not create it either. The gating checkpoint is `tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase4.py`, and this step is production code only.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\ntests/tmp/probe_09_phase4_impl.py - a throwaway probe of the upnext_pool line on the implemented phase. I have no tool that deletes files, so it is still on disk and needs removing (as do the earlier probe_09_* files noted in previous steps).\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "step_8_i1_refactor": "<refactors>\nengine/server/data/similarity_candidates.py - the seed-embedding normalisation was the same six lines in `get_similar_candidates` and `get_upnext_candidates`; moved it into one new `_seed_with_embedding(seed)` helper, which returns the seed with `embedding` set (falling back to `vector`) or None. Both callers keep their own early return ([] and ([], stats)), so behaviour is unchanged.\nengine/server/api/server_config.py - updated the `enabled` comment above RELATED_VIDEOS_PERSONALIZATION to say it reranks the up-next top-M window and that the reranked score is the draw weight and page order. Phase 1 deliberately held this back until the window existed, which it now does after phase 4. Comment only.\n</refactors>\n\n<left_out>\nThe floor in `_upnext_rows` is now redundant, since every caller passes entries already at or above tail_min_score (cached entries are floored first and `search_similar_above` floors its hits). I kept it as the pool's own guarantee: without it, a future caller could let rows below the floor into an up-next page. Removing it would not change behaviour today.\n`compute_similar_items` and `search_similar_above` in data/ann.py both normalise the query vector. I did not share that code: it is two lines, and one of the functions was there before this build.\n`_author_key` is defined in both ann.py and similarity_candidates.py, and `_build_rows` checks `author_limit > 0 and author_key` twice. Both are older than this build, so not part of this pass.\nIn `_handle_seed_with_embedding`, the inner `penalise(candidates, settings)` shadows the outer `settings`. It is a mechanical move and every branch maps one to one, but the phase checkpoints (tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1..4.py) have not been re-run on it.\nThe step's \"What the pass is measured against\" section arrived as an unfilled `{rat_tail_rules}` placeholder. I worked from the rat-tail rule in my role instead. I found no new simplification that needs a rat-tail comment.\n</left_out>\n\n<needs_fresh_red>\nNot behaviour I could add in a refactor, but the build is incomplete. tests/active/test_upnext_diversity.py was never created: the gating tests are still in tests/tmp/test_09_similars_diversity_phase1..4.py. The pinned rewrites planned for phase 2 were never written either: conftest `upnext_pool`/`pin_upnext` and the changes to test_similar, test_dislike_profile, test_blocks, test_dislikes, test_frontend_blocks and test_frontend_videos. Those durable tests compare unseeded up-next requests, and those pages are now random draws. Phase 2 already reported that test_frontend_videos breaks, because a 48-row pool no longer produces an empty batch within 6. These need a test-authoring step before the build can close. The probe files tests/tmp/probe_09_*.py (and their __pycache__) also still need deleting; I have no delete tool.\n</needs_fresh_red>\n\n<observation>\nThe production code for all four phases is coherent and needed only two small refactors (one duplicated seed-normalisation block, one stale comment). The real gap is on the test side: the durable up-next test file and the pinned rewrites of the six existing active tests never landed.\n</observation>",

    "step_8_triage:1": "<failures>\n### test_frontend_videos::test_the_pager_s_batches_never_repeat_a_row_and_it_stops_asking_after_an_empty_batch\n**Cause.** The test fails at its own control on line 87, `plain_a[\"plain\"] == plain_b[\"plain\"]` (\"a plain fetch does not repeat\"). The run shows the two plain fetches' first rows as `d63cb157\u2026@video.linux.it` and `58198c28\u2026@makertube.net`. Phase 3 C1 makes each up-next page a random score-weighted draw, so two plain fetches no longer return the same page. The test also conflicts with phase 2 C1 further down: line 101 needs an empty batch within MAX_BATCHES = 6 batches of 8, but the linux pool is now filled past 48 rows, so no batch comes back empty.\n**Fault.** The test. It was built on the assumption that up-next is deterministic and the pool is shallow (\"19 deep when measured\"). This build confirmed two requirements that remove both assumptions. Neither is an implementation regression.\n**What changed.** In the previous step-8 turn the operator chose \"Retire them now\", and this test was retired whole to `tests/archive/upnext_random_draw/test_frontend_videos.py`. That copy is verbatim, apart from a provenance docstring, `pytestmark = skip` and `parents[3]`. Issue 35 (`docs/project/issues/35-upnext-tests-retired-by-random-draw.md`) tracks its replacement. That turn could not delete the active copy, so it stayed in `tests/active` and kept this run red. This turn, the operator deleted `tests/active/test_frontend_videos.py` at my request. Glob confirms the archive copy is now the only one. No test was edited or weakened.\n\n### The other groups in this run\nAll six are green: test_blocks 3, test_dislike_profile 5, test_dislikes 2, test_frontend_blocks 1, test_search_fusion 10, test_similar 25. The 19 \"gone\" entries in the compare are exactly the tests and parametrized cases that the last step-8 turn retired to `tests/archive/upnext_random_draw/`. None was lost by accident. This turn changed none of them.\n</failures>\n\n<checkpoint_gaps>\n- **Phase 2.** Its checkpoint said the four pinned rewrites, test_frontend_videos among them, \"land here and must pass\". The gate ran only the tests/tmp checkpoint, and the implementer left every listed test file untouched. test_frontend_videos broke for certain in this phase, because the pool reached 48 or more rows and so no 8-row batch came back empty. The phase outcome predicted that failure, but it was never gated. Phase 2's checkpoint should have caught it.\n- **Phase 3.** Its checkpoint said \"the full suite, including the pinned rewrites from phase 2, must stay green now that the draws are random\", but only the tmp diversity checkpoint ran. The random draw that breaks line 87's plain-repeat control was introduced here. Phase 3's checkpoint should have caught it.\n- **Harness, carried from the previous step-8 turn.** `.un/skills/devsecops/config.json` still maps a `test_frontend_videos.py` group that no longer has a file. It also maps no Engine file to test_blocks, test_dislikes or test_frontend_blocks (plan \u00a77i). Both belong to harvest's map update. Issue 35 records both.\n</checkpoint_gaps>\n\n<correction>\n1. Inspected the failing test first. Its red is the control at line 87, which requires two plain up-next fetches to be identical. That conflicts with phase 3 C1, and line 101 conflicts with phase 2 C1. It is a test fault; the implementation is not at fault.\n2. Read the session record. The previous step-8 turn had already retired this test with the operator's approval (\"Retire them now\") and archived it to `tests/archive/upnext_random_draw/test_frontend_videos.py`. It asked the operator to delete the active copy, which it could not do itself. The active copy was still on disk, and it is the only red in this run.\n3. Checked `validate_tests.py` to see whether emptying the file in place would be enough. It would not: a lane that collects nothing exits 5, is treated as undescribed, and never banks green. So the file had to be deleted, not overwritten, and I left its bytes alone.\n4. Asked the operator to delete `tests/active/test_frontend_videos.py`. The answer was \"deleted\", and Glob confirms the only copy left is the archived one.\n5. Touched no production file, no checkpoint (`tests/tmp/test_09_*`) and no active test this turn. I ran no probe and no suite, so `tests/last_test_validation.json` stands as the workflow wrote it.\n\n**Still for the operator or harvest.**\n- Drop the `test_frontend_videos.py` entry from `.un/skills/devsecops/config.json`, as issue 35 says.\n- Delete the emptied step-8 probes `tests/tmp/probe_09_step8_home_pair.py` and `tests/tmp/probe_09_step8_blocks_vacuity.py`, and the earlier `tests/tmp/probe_09_*` leftovers.\n- Re-run the workflow's `--compare` to confirm the suite is green now that the file is gone.\n</correction>",
    "step_9_triage": "<docs>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md\" update=\"yes\">\nSeveral sentences on up-next are now false.\n- \u00a71 \"Up Next\" (lines 11-12) says up-next \"reorders similar items via local scoring\". That no longer describes what is served. It should say:\n  - the routes are POST `/recommendations?id=&host=`, POST `/videos/similar` and GET `/videos/{id}/similar`;\n  - the pool is scored and dislike-penalised;\n  - the top M = `SIMILAR_VIDEO_SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR` (4) \u00d7 limit rows form the window, capped at the pool size;\n  - `limit` rows are drawn from the window by score-weighted Efraimidis\u2013Spirakis sampling without replacement, afresh on each request;\n  - a window of `limit` rows or fewer is returned whole;\n  - the page is ordered by the draw weight, descending;\n  - the optional integer `seed` query parameter makes the draw reproducible. It is Engine-only, because the Client gateway answers 400 for an unknown query parameter.\n- \u00a71 \"Excluded Videos\" (line 27) says up-next excluded rows \"are removed after ranking and before the page is cut\". It should say they are removed while the pool is built, before scoring and the window, so the next page is drawn from rows not yet shown.\n- \u00a72 item 3 \"Similarity cache\" (lines 36-39) describes only the home behaviour of refreshing and recomputing. It should add the up-next side:\n  - up-next reads the cache but never writes it, so it no longer warms the cache for seeds it has not seen;\n  - up-next drops cached rows below `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TAIL_MIN_SCORE` (0.25);\n  - a pool below `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TARGET_MIN_POOL` (= `BATCH_SIZE`, 48), or a missing cache entry, runs a live ANN fallback. It starts at nprobe 32 / k 5000 and doubles both up to 128 / 20000. It stops at the target, at both caps, or when a step adds no row;\n  - hits at 0.35 or above are added first, then a 0.25\u20130.35 tail only if the pool is still short;\n  - the pool is deduped by `(video_uuid, instance_domain)` and `like_key` and capped at `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TOP_K` (300);\n  - nprobe is set and restored within one `index_lock` hold;\n  - `refresh_cache` on up-next skips the cache read and forces the fallback instead of rewriting the entry;\n  - the floors apply to PQ-approximate scores.\n- \u00a75 \"Dislike penalty\" (line 118) says up-next applies it \"before ranking; the related-videos personalization keeps the full penalty\". It should say:\n  - on up-next the penalty applies over the whole pool before the window;\n  - with likes, `rerank_related_videos` (alpha 0.7 / beta 0.3) runs on the window before the draw;\n  - its `personalized_score` is the draw weight and the page order, keeping the full penalty.\n- \u00a78 (line 140) still holds.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/LAYER_PARAMS.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe file has no up-next section, and \"Source Params (Hard Limits)\" (lines 60-68) reads as if `DEFAULT_SIMILAR_PER_LIKE`, `DEFAULT_SIMILARITY_SEARCH_LIMIT` and `DEFAULT_SIMILARITY_REQUIRE_FULL_CACHE` govern every similarity read.\n- Add an up-next section listing the nine `server_config.py` constants with their defaults and meaning:\n  - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_SEARCH_LIMIT` 5000;\n  - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TOP_K` 300;\n  - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_NPROBE` 32;\n  - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TARGET_MIN_POOL` = `BATCH_SIZE`, so it follows the home profile's `batch_size`;\n  - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_NPROBE` 128;\n  - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT` 20000;\n  - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_MIN_SCORE` 0.35;\n  - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TAIL_MIN_SCORE` 0.25;\n  - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR` 4.\n- In the same section, cover `RELATED_VIDEOS_PERSONALIZATION` (alpha 0.7 / beta 0.3, `max_likes`), applied to the top-M window, with its score used as the draw weight.\n- Note that `DEFAULT_SIMILAR_PER_LIKE` is still the up-next cache read limit, taken as the maximum of it and TOP_K.\n- At lines 60-68, say that these params and `DEFAULT_NPROBE` govern the home layers, and that up-next always reads the cache with require_full off and never writes it.\n- Note that the server-wide `DEFAULT_SIMILARITY_CACHE_REFRESH` makes every up-next request skip the cache and run the fallback.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/PIPELINE_DIAGRAM.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe diagram routes the upnext branch (line 11) through the layer pipeline and the \"Similarity cache ... refresh if score missing\" node (line 19). Neither is how up-next is served.\n- Add a separate up-next branch: cache read (never written) \u2192 tail floor, `_build_rows` (seed, error, author caps), exclude, moderation \u2192 ANN fallback steps (floor 0.35, then tail 0.25), dedup, cap 300 \u2192 score + dislike penalty \u2192 top-M window \u2192 likes rerank \u2192 weighted draw (random or `seed`) \u2192 page sorted by draw weight.\n- Line 3 names a `RECOMMENDATIONS_OVERVIEW.md` that does not exist. Point it at `docs/OVERVIEW.md`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/README.md\" update=\"yes\">\nNext to the `debug=1` bullet (line 24), add a bullet on the optional `seed` query parameter on `/recommendations?id=`, `/videos/similar` and `GET /videos/{id}/similar`. It should say:\n- a non-negative integer reproduces an up-next draw for the same pool;\n- a missing, negative or non-integer value means a random draw, not a 400;\n- without it, up-next pages vary per request;\n- the Client gateway does not forward it and answers 400 `Unknown query parameter: seed`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"DEPLOYMENT.md\" update=\"yes\">\n- **\u00a77 debug toggle (line 419).** Mention `seed=<int>` for reproducing an up-next page, sent directly to the Engine only.\n- **Logs.** Document three lines:\n  - the startup line `[similar-server] upnext_config SEARCH_LIMIT=\u2026 SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR=\u2026`, logged next to `ann_nprobe_configured`;\n  - the per-request `[similar-server][<id>] upnext_pool initial= steps= restored_nprobe= final= tail= sampling= window= likes_rerank= returned=` line;\n  - the `ann_fallback` line.\n- **Capacity.** Until the precompute top-k is raised, nearly every up-next request runs a live ANN fallback: up to three searches, reaching nprobe 128 / k 20000, under the global `index_lock` that home and search share. The request deadline does not cover FAISS, so an overrun surfaces at the next DB statement as a 500.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"DATA_BUILD.md\" update=\"yes\">\nStep 5 precompute `--top-k 20` (lines 240-246): add that up-next makes up for these shallow entries with a serve-time ANN fallback on every seed whose filtered pool is under 48. Raising `--top-k` and rebuilding `similarity-cache.db` is the upgrade path that removes that per-request cost.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/09-similars-diversity.md\" update=\"yes\">\nAt harvest, set `Status: enhancement, complete`, add a delivery comment and move the file to `docs/project/issues/archive/`. The delivery comment records:\n- `/api/similar` does not exist, and up-next is the three seeded routes;\n- `get_upnext_candidates` and `search_similar_above` run a live ANN on short pools and never write the cache, so up-next no longer warms it;\n- the draw uses linear score weights (E\u2013S), cached rows are floored at 0.25, and the 0.35/0.25 floors apply to PQ-approximate scores;\n- `refresh_cache` forces the fallback;\n- `seed` is Engine-only;\n- personalization runs at alpha 0.7 / beta 0.3 on the window;\n- the `upnext_pool` log line exists;\n- the durable up-next tests that assumed deterministic pages were retired to `tests/archive/upnext_random_draw/`, and their replacement is issue 35;\n- plan 17 must migrate `search_similar_above` and the nprobe helpers now in `data/ann.py`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/11-fast-similars-response.md\" update=\"yes\">\nAdd a comment. Up-next now pays up to three live ANN searches per request under `index_lock` (nprobe up to 128, k up to 20000) plus larger metadata and dislike-embedding fetches for a pool of up to 300. This is the latency this issue cares about. Raising the precompute `--top-k` and rebuilding the cache removes most of it.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/plan.md\" update=\"yes\">\n- **Row 2a (line 70).** Mark it delivered. Extend its file list with `data/ann.py`, `api/server.py` and `recommendations/related_personalization.py`. Note that the deterministic up-next tests were retired, with issue 35 tracking their replacement; they were not rewritten, as the checklist assumed.\n- **Row 5a (line 99).** Note that `data/ann.py` now also holds `search_similar_above` and the nprobe helpers (`_extract_ivf`, `get_nprobe`, `apply_nprobe`, `set_nprobe`), which 08 must migrate.\n- **Line 132 (08 vs 09).** Still accurate: 09 kept rowid ids and added one more rowid reader in the one file. Nothing to change there.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/plans/17-stable-ann-ids.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe inventory at line 19 lists only `compute_similar_items` and `search_index` in `data/ann.py`. Add `search_similar_above`: it takes rowid hits, applies the `ids > 0` filter, excludes `seed[\"rowid\"]` and calls `fetch_metadata` by rowid. Also note that the Engine's nprobe helpers moved from `server.py` into `data/ann.py`. The copy in `precompute-similar-ann.py` is still separate.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/issues/12-similars-on-scroll.md\" update=\"yes\">\nNot on the checklist. This issue builds directly on what 09 delivered, and its plan (line 14: \"the server returns a full batch \u2026 `BATCH_SIZE = 48`\") must know that each up-next response is now a random draw. Add a comment saying:\n- a limit-48 request draws 48 from a window of min(192, pool \u2264 300);\n- scroll paging therefore has to exclude shown rows, as `createFeedPager` does, rather than rely on a repeatable page;\n- the frontend pager test that covered this was retired (issue 35).\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/roadmap.md\" update=\"yes\">\nNot on the checklist. The \"Delivered\" section lists delivered issue work, and issue 09 is now delivered. Add a Delivered line for issue 09 (up-next pools filled past one batch by a serve-time ANN fallback, a score-weighted random draw per refresh, likes reranking at alpha 0.7 / beta 0.3), pointing at `docs/project/plans/19-09-similars-diversity.md`. F4-M3 (line 56) can keep its reference to issue 09.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/adr/0006-derived-ann-ids.md\" update=\"no\">\nThe ADR decides the id scheme that plan 17 will introduce. This build keeps today's rowid ids, as the operator confirmed, and puts its one new ANN reader in `data/ann.py`, where plan 17 migrates it. `search_similar_above` drops ids \u2264 0, which matches decision 3. Nothing in the ADR is made false; the extra migration surface is recorded in plan 17.\n</doc>\n</docs>\n\n<adr_conflicts>\nnone\n</adr_conflicts>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md": "<changes>\nOVERVIEW.md now describes how up-next is actually served: a pool that only reads the cache, the ANN fallback when the pool is short, a top-M window and a weighted random draw.\n\nI checked each claim against `handlers/similar.py`, `data/similarity_candidates.py`, `data/similarity_cache_manager.py` and `recommendations/related_personalization.py`.\n\n- **\u00a71 \"Up Next\":** lists the three seeded routes: POST `/recommendations?id=&host=`, POST `/videos/similar` and GET `/videos/{id}/similar`. The pool is scored with the `upnext` profile and gets the dislike penalty. The window is the top `SIMILAR_VIDEO_SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR` \u00d7 `limit` rows, capped at the pool size. `limit` rows are drawn from it by score-weighted Efraimidis\u2013Spirakis sampling without replacement, afresh on each request. A window of `limit` rows or fewer is returned whole, and the page is ordered by draw weight, descending. The `seed` query parameter makes the draw reproducible and only the Engine accepts it; its parse rules and the gateway's 400 are left to `engine/server/README.md`.\n- **\u00a71 \"Excluded Videos\":** on up-next, excluded rows are removed while the pool is built, before scoring and the window, so the next page is drawn from rows not yet shown.\n- **\u00a72 \"Similarity cache\":** new up-next part:\n  - up-next reads the cache and never writes it, so it does not warm the cache for new seeds;\n  - cached rows below the tail floor are dropped, then the seed, error, per-author, exclude and moderation filters apply;\n  - the ANN fallback runs when the pool is short or the seed has no cache entry, with its start values, doubling steps, caps and three stop conditions;\n  - hits above the floor are added first, then the tail only if the pool is still short;\n  - the pool is deduplicated by `(video_uuid, instance_domain)` and `like_key` (the cached row wins a clash) and capped at `TOP_K`;\n  - nprobe is set and restored within one `index_lock` hold;\n  - `refresh_cache` skips the cache read and forces the fallback, without rewriting the entry;\n  - the score floors compare against PQ-approximate ANN scores.\n- **\u00a75 \"Dislike penalty\":** on up-next the penalty applies over the whole pool, before the window. With likes, `rerank_related_videos` then reranks the window before the draw. Its `personalized_score` is the draw weight and the page order, and it keeps the full penalty.\n\nI named the constants but left out their values. The checklist asked for numbers like 0.25, 48 and 300 in this file, but `LAYER_PARAMS.md` owns the defaults (including alpha 0.7 / beta 0.3), so \u00a72 points there instead.\n\n\u00a78 is unchanged: the `seed` field it describes is the response's mode, not the query parameter.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/LAYER_PARAMS.md": "<changes>\nI added an \"Up-next Params\" section to LAYER_PARAMS.md and a note that the Source Params govern only the home layers.\n\n- **Source Params (Hard Limits):** a new paragraph under the list says these params and `DEFAULT_NPROBE` govern the home layers. It links to the up-next section. It says up-next always reads the similarity cache with require_full off and never writes it, whatever `DEFAULT_SIMILARITY_REQUIRE_FULL_CACHE` is set to. It also notes that the per-author cap, the exclude-source-author setting and `VIDEO_ERROR_THRESHOLD` apply to the up-next pool too.\n- **New \"Up-next Params\" section** at the end of the file:\n  - An intro says up-next does not run the layers. The `upnext` / `guest_upnext` profile supplies only the scoring weights. The pool mechanics are described in `OVERVIEW.md` \u00a7 1 and \u00a7 2, and the intro points there instead of repeating them.\n  - \"Pool and ANN Fallback\" lists these constants with their defaults and what each does:\n    - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_SEARCH_LIMIT`, `SIMILAR_VIDEO_NPROBE`, `SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT`, `SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_NPROBE`, `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TOP_K`, `SIMILAR_VIDEO_MIN_SCORE` and `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TAIL_MIN_SCORE`;\n    - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_TARGET_MIN_POOL`, which equals `BATCH_SIZE` and so follows the home `batch_size`;\n    - `DEFAULT_SIMILAR_PER_LIKE`, which sets the cache read limit as `max(\u2026, TOP_K)`;\n    - `DEFAULT_SIMILARITY_CACHE_REFRESH` and the per-request `refresh_cache`, which make up-next skip the cache read and run the fallback.\n  - \"Window and Draw\" covers two settings:\n    - `SIMILAR_VIDEO_SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR` (the top-M window);\n    - `RELATED_VIDEOS_PERSONALIZATION` (alpha 0.7 / beta 0.3 / `max_likes` 5). It reranks the window before the draw, and the reranked score becomes both the draw weight and the page order.\n\nI checked every value and behaviour against the code: `server_config.py:309-377`, `get_upnext_candidates` in `data/similarity_candidates.py`, `_handle_seed_with_embedding` and the `refresh_cache` parse in `handlers/similar.py`, and the rerank formula in `related_personalization.py:88`. The rerank weights the row's ranked `score` by alpha, not the raw source similarity, and keeps the full dislike penalty; the section says so.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/PIPELINE_DIAGRAM.md": "<changes>\nThe diagram now shows up-next as its own branch, separate from the home layer pipeline, and the broken overview link is fixed.\n\n- **Intro line:** it now points at `engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md`; `RECOMMENDATIONS_OVERVIEW.md` does not exist. The line also says the home feed runs the layer pipeline while up-next draws its page from one similarity pool. It sends readers to `LAYER_PARAMS.md` for the up-next parameters, which that file owns.\n- **Node D (upnext):** it names the upnext profile, or guest_upnext when there are no likes, and the other two seeded routes (`/videos/similar`, `GET /videos/{id}/similar`). The `D --> E` edge is gone because up-next doesn't go through the layer pipeline, and the home likes node E2 now reads \"Use home profile\".\n- **New up-next branch (U1\u2013U10):**\n  - The similarity cache is read but never written, and the read is skipped when `refresh_cache` is set.\n  - Pool filters: the 0.25 tail floor, seed, error and author caps, the request's exclude keys, then moderation.\n  - The ANN fallback runs when the pool is below `TARGET_MIN_POOL` or the cache has no entry. It steps nprobe 32\u2192128 and k 5000\u219220000, adds hits at 0.35 or above first and then the 0.25 tail, and restores nprobe under `index_lock`.\n  - The pool is deduped by `(video_uuid, instance_domain)` and `like_key`, then capped at 300.\n  - Scoring and the dislike penalty run over the whole pool.\n  - The window is the top M rows, M = `SAMPLE_WINDOW_FACTOR` \u00d7 limit.\n  - With likes, the rerank (alpha 0.7 / beta 0.3) runs on the window and stamps `personalized_score`.\n  - `limit` rows are drawn by Efraimidis\u2013Spirakis weighting, randomly or reproducibly with `seed`.\n  - The page is sorted by draw weight, and the request writes its `upnext_pool` log line.\n- I checked each node against `get_upnext_candidates`, `_upnext_rows` and `_dedup_rows` in `data/similarity_candidates.py`, and against `_handle_seed_with_embedding` and `_draw_page` in `handlers/similar.py`. I haven't rendered the diagram to check the Mermaid syntax.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/README.md": "<changes>\nAdded a Notes bullet for the up-next `seed` query parameter, placed after the `debug=1` bullet.\n\n- **Routes:** it applies to `/recommendations?id=`, `/videos/similar` and `GET /videos/{id}/similar`.\n- **With a non-negative integer:** the draw can be repeated, and the same pool returns the same page.\n- **Without it:** each up-next request draws a different page.\n- **Missing, negative or non-integer value:** the draw is random and the Engine does not answer 400. The code confirms this: `_parse_non_negative_int` returns None for these values, and None means a random draw in `_draw_page`, in `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py`.\n- **Engine only:** the Client gateway does not forward `seed` and answers 400 `Unknown query parameter: seed`. The code confirms this: `seed` is not in `PROXY_ALLOWED_QUERY_PARAMS`, and the parameter is rejected in `client/backend/server.py:423` and `:478`.\n- **Link instead of repeat:** how the page is drawn (the window, the Efraimidis\u2013Spirakis draw, the ordering) belongs to `engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md`, so the bullet links there instead of restating it.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DEPLOYMENT.md": "<changes>\nDEPLOYMENT.md: added the up-next log lines, the fallback's load and timeout risk, and how `seed=<int>` reproduces a page.\n\n- **New \u00a74 subsection \"Up-next logs and load\".**\n  - It names the three up-next routes and points to `recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md` for how the pool is built and drawn.\n  - It documents three log lines:\n    - the startup `[similar-server] upnext_config \u2026` line, logged right after `ann_nprobe_configured`. Its tokens use the full `SIMILAR_VIDEO_*` names, as `server.py:347` writes them.\n    - the `ann_fallback nprobe= search_limit= floor= hits= restored_nprobe=` line, logged once per live search.\n    - the per-request `[similar-server][<id>] upnext_pool \u2026` line, including the formats of `steps` and `sampling`.\n  - A capacity paragraph covers the cost of the shallow cache. The cache holds 20 rows per seed (pointed at `DATA_BUILD.md`), so nearly every up-next request runs the fallback: up to three searches, from nprobe 32 / k 5000 up to 128 / 20000, under the shared `index_lock`.\n  - The same paragraph says the 5 s request deadline bounds only SQLite work, not FAISS. A request whose searches overrun it fails at its next DB statement with `500 Recommendations request failed`.\n- **\u00a77, after the debug toggle.** Up-next pages are a random draw. `seed=<int>` reproduces a page, needs no toggle, and must be sent to the Engine directly. The Client backend answers `400 Unknown query parameter: seed`.\n\nChecked against the code:\n- The log formats are in `data/ann.py:119`, `handlers/similar.py:1134` and `server.py:347`.\n- `seed` is missing from `PROXY_ALLOWED_QUERY_PARAMS` (`client/backend/server.py:86-87`).\n- The deadline is `DEFAULT_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5.0`. The generic `except Exception` in the similar handler (`similar.py:1049`) catches the interrupted-statement error first, so the answer is a 500 and not the 503 timeout.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DATA_BUILD.md": "<changes>\nStep 5 of DATA_BUILD.md now says that `--top-k 20` entries are too shallow for up-next, which fills the gap with a serve-time ANN fallback, and that raising `--top-k` and rebuilding the cache is the fix.\n\n- I added one paragraph after the \"This output is large\" note in step 5.
